problem: World model-based planning is computationally expensive in resource-constrained robotics environments, making real-time deployment infeasible.
approach: The paper uses a sparsely trained vision-based transformer world model with randomized grouped attention to reduce token processing during forward prediction, enabling flexible adjustment of computational resources during latent rollout.
contribution: Sparse imagination maintains task performance while dramatically improving inference efficiency, enabling deployment of world models in real-time robotics scenarios.

problem: Existing reward model benchmarks do not correlate well with downstream performance despite being used to evaluate reward models used in LLM post-training.
approach: RewardEval introduces a multi-skill reward modeling benchmark with new human prompts and challenging data, showing 20-point lower average scores than RewardBench and correlating with downstream performance in inference-time and training-time settings.
contribution: RewardEval provides rigorous evaluation practices and demonstrates how reward model performance on the benchmark correlates with effectiveness in best-of-N sampling and RLHF training.

problem: Knowledge editing methods require resource-heavy backpropagation incompatible with mobile devices, preventing on-device LLM personalization.
approach: MobiEdit replaces full-precision backpropagation with quantized forward-only gradient estimation compatible with mobile neural processing units, adding early stopping and prefix activation reusing optimizations.
contribution: MobiEdit enables real-time editing of 3B-parameter models on commercial mobile devices with 7.1x less memory, 15.8x less energy, and 3.4x less latency.

problem: Existing benchmarks assess verbal reasoning alone, not the multi-step visual simulation skills essential for spatial cognition.
approach: STARE introduces a 3K-task benchmark spanning 2D/3D geometric transformations, cube net folding, tangram puzzles, and real-world spatial reasoning, evaluating multimodal LLMs on complex visual simulation.
contribution: Evaluations reveal models perform near random chance on complex spatial tasks requiring multi-step visual simulation, while humans achieve near-perfect accuracy despite longer completion times.

problem: Hardware-aware neural architecture search methods struggle to satisfy hardware constraints without introducing hyperparameter tuning and differentiability requirements.
approach: ConNAS enforces hardware constraints directly through gradient modification of architectural choices, steering the search toward feasible architectures without regularization terms or differentiable hardware metrics.
contribution: ConNAS discovers architectures meeting hardware constraints while achieving performance within 0.14% of optimal feasible architectures and outperforming handcrafted designs by up to 1.55% under tight budgets.

problem: Standard deep generative models with learned encoders and variational bounds struggle to produce low-dimensional, interpretable embeddings of high-dimensional data.
approach: QLVMs directly approximate marginal likelihood using randomized quasi-Monte Carlo integration to find one-, two-, and three-dimensional interpretable embeddings, enabling transparent visualization and post-hoc analysis.
contribution: QLVMs consistently outperform VAEs and IWAEs with matched latent dimensionality, enabling nonparametric density estimation, clustering, and geodesic path computation in interpretable low-dimensional spaces.

problem: Existing API-based benchmarks use isolated tools and explicit specifications, not capturing realistic multi-step tasks requiring cross-tool coordination and planning.
approach: MCP-Bench connects LLMs to 28 live MCP servers spanning 250 tools via the Model Context Protocol, constructing authentic multi-step tasks that require tool retrieval, planning, and cross-domain workflows.
contribution: Experiments on 20 advanced LLMs reveal persistent challenges in tool-level schema understanding, trajectory planning, and cross-domain task completion.

problem: Prior convergence analysis of Tsetlin Machines covers only 1-bit and 2-bit XOR operators under noise-free conditions, lacking comprehensive theory for general k-bit settings and noise.
approach: The paper extends analysis to 2-bit AND and OR operators under noisy and noise-free training, then generalizes to k-bit settings with unified treatment of convergence properties.
contribution: Provides robust theoretical foundation showing TM converges almost surely under noise-free training and that mislabeled samples permit efficient learning while irrelevant variables do not prevent convergence.

problem: Traffic models struggle to jointly capture microscopic vehicle interactions and macroscopic flow evolution without requiring historical trajectories.
approach: MMCKM lifts coupled micro-macro dynamics to a high-dimensional linear space using Koopman operators with scenario-adaptive evolvers and explicit macro-to-micro control modules on vehicle-centric dynamic graphs.
contribution: Achieves comparable or higher trajectory prediction accuracy than history-dependent baselines using only real-time measurement on NGSIM and HighD datasets.

problem: Standard CNNs are sensitive to photometric variations and data augmentation alone cannot provide formal guarantees of robustness.
approach: SEqSI achieves intensity scale equivariance and shift invariance by design through a shift-invariant layer prepended to a scale-equivariant backbone, providing certified affine transformation invariance.
contribution: SEqSI provides formal robustness guarantees to affine intensity transformations and enhances generalization on image classification and object localization across photometric corruptions and domain shifts.

problem: 3D few-shot class-incremental learning requires balancing novel-class adaptation against preserving base-class knowledge without explicit retraining.
approach: Point-UQ uses uncertainty quantification to dynamically arbitrate between semantic classifiers and geometric prototypes via Attention-driven Adaptive Enhancement and Uncertainty-quantification Decision Decoupling modules.
contribution: Enables robust base-class knowledge retention and accurate novel-class recognition in 3D few-shot incremental learning without retraining on ModelNet, ShapeNet, and other point-cloud benchmarks.

problem: Current evaluation of ML papers conflates rhetorical style with substantive content, making it unclear whether bold language reflects genuine evidence or mere hype.
approach: An LLM-based framework generates counterfactual writings from the same substantive content using multiple personas, aggregates pairwise LLM judgments via Bradley-Terry model to isolate rhetorical style.
contribution: Analysis of 8,485 ICLR submissions reveals visionary framing predicts citations and media coverage independent of peer review, and rhetorical strength increased sharply after 2023 correlated with LLM writing assistance adoption.

problem: Existing SFT approaches for LLM-based human behavior simulation are bounded by the reasoning capabilities of the model generating synthetic rationales.
approach: Shop-R1 uses RL with two-stage decomposition: self-supervised internal-signal guidance for rationale generation and hierarchical difficulty-aware reward scaling for action prediction to prevent reward hacking.
contribution: Achieves 65% relative improvement over baselines in predicting real human behavior in online shopping environments.

problem: Diffusion models lack access to marginal densities along generation trajectories, limiting their application to inference-time control and energy-based training.
approach: RNE (Radon-Nikodym Estimator) uses density ratios between path distributions to reveal connections between marginal densities and transition kernels, providing a unified framework for diffusion density estimation, control, and training.
contribution: RNE delivers strong results in inference-time control applications like annealing and model composition with promising inference-time scaling, and provides efficient regularization for energy-based diffusion training.

problem: KL-regularized RL objectives may induce diversity collapse when targeting high-reward regions under common settings like low regularization strength.
approach: Analysis shows target distributions under forward and reverse KL regularization concentrate on single high-reward regions; the paper proposes rescaling rewards to induce broad probability mass across all high-reward regions.
contribution: The modified objective maintains high solution quality while achieving broad reward-mode coverage, improving post-training diversity for LLMs and Chemical Language Models.

problem: VLMs struggle with fine-grained image classification despite extensive text knowledge, failing to differentiate visually similar categories.
approach: DiVE-k leverages model top-k predictions as training signals, creating multiple-choice questions from top outputs and using RL to train fine-grained differential reasoning without memorization.
contribution: Outperforms existing approaches by 10.04% and 6.16% on Harmonic Mean metric in base-to-novel generalization on five fine-grained datasets.

problem: Quantifying subjective value alignment for which no ground-truth labels exist remains an open problem.
approach: EigenBench uses an ensemble of models as judges to evaluate each other across scenarios according to a constitution, aggregating judgments via EigenTrust to produce consensus scores without ground-truth labels.
contribution: EigenBench's rankings align closely with human evaluators and can recover GPQA benchmark rankings without objective labels, providing a framework for evaluating subjective model values.

problem: Lightweight 3D medical image segmentation faces an efficiency-robustness conflict when handling complex anatomies and heterogeneous modalities.
approach: VeloxSeg uses a dual-stream CNN-Transformer with Paired Window Attention for rapid multi-scale retrieval and Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma-guided convolution for robust local features; Spatially Decoupled Knowledge Transfer injects texture priors.
contribution: Achieves 26% Dice improvement with 11x GPU throughput increase, 48x CPU increase, and 1/24 inference memory reduction on multimodal benchmarks.

problem: The assumption that personalizing ML models improves both prediction and explanation accuracy remains largely unvalidated.
approach: A unified framework quantifies whether personalization improves prediction and explanation for demographic groups, derives finite-sample error bounds on hypothesis tests, and applies to real-world tabular data.
contribution: Demonstrates prediction and explanation impacts can diverge; identifies scenarios where effects are fundamentally untestable due to dataset statistics.

problem: Local flatness alone does not guarantee better generalization in domain generalization; a global geometric property is needed.
approach: BOA (Billiard Optimization Algorithm) discovers superior models by traversing connected pathways between local minima in a low-dimensional Krylov subspace, mimicking billiard dynamics.
contribution: BOA consistently outperforms sharpness-aware and domain generalization methods across DomainBed, even surpassing oracle-aware baselines.

problem: Autoregressive video diffusion models cannot guide generation with future conditioning, causing collisions with generated scenes in camera-guided video generation.
approach: GVS samples entire sequences in parallel using diffusion stitching compatible with models trained via Diffusion Forcing; OmniGuidance conditions on both past and future with loop-closing for coherence.
contribution: Achieves stable, collision-free, frame-to-frame consistent camera-guided video generation that closes loops for diverse predefined camera paths.

problem: VLMs lack 3D spatial reasoning ability for multi-view, ego-centric observations typical in embodied AI systems.
approach: Ego3D-Bench comprises 8,600 QA pairs from ego-centric multi-view outdoor data; Ego3D-VLM generates cognitive maps from estimated global 3D coordinates via post-training.
contribution: VLMs show performance gaps relative to humans; Ego3D-VLM improves multi-choice QA by 12% and distance estimation by 56%.

problem: Retrieved context in RAG remains unstructured, limiting multi-step reasoning in knowledge-intensive tasks.
approach: RAS (Retrieval-And-Structuring) dynamically constructs question-specific knowledge graphs through iterative retrieval and structured knowledge building, interleaving targeted retrieval planning with incremental graph construction.
contribution: Achieves up to 8.7% and 7.0% gains over baselines on seven knowledge-intensive benchmarks with proprietary and open-source LLMs respectively.

problem: Survival analysis methods focus on predictive accuracy and concordance but neglect fine-grained calibration.
approach: ICALD unifies parametric and nonparametric survival modeling via the Individually Calibrated Asymmetric Laplace Distribution with quantile regression loss, supporting both pre- and post-calibration strategies.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance in accuracy, concordance, and calibration, outperforming 12 existing baselines including recent pre- and post-calibration methods on synthetic and real-world datasets.

problem: Trillion-scale pre-training dataset selection rarely considers quality and diversity metrics jointly due to high computational cost and diminishing returns.
approach: DataMask frames selection as mask learning via policy gradients, iteratively sampling data masks and updating mask logits to simultaneously optimize quality and diversity metrics.
contribution: Reduces selection time by 98.9% compared to greedy algorithms, enabling exploration of joint optimization.

problem: Safety evaluations of LLMs miss targeted vulnerabilities and current steering methods enable broad but not selective suppression of refusal.
approach: RepIt enables selective suppression of refusal on targeted concepts while preserving refusal elsewhere through concept-specific representation isolation and steering vector modification affecting only 100-200 neurons.
contribution: Produces evaluation-evading models answering questions on weapons while scoring safe on standard benchmarks with minimal resources, exposing vulnerabilities in current safety evaluation practices.

problem: Existing language agent memory systems lack episodic recollection and reasoning capabilities, focusing instead on semantic memory and simple retrieval.
approach: REMem constructs a hybrid time-aware memory graph during offline indexing and employs an agentic retriever with curated tools for iterative online reasoning over episodic events.
contribution: Outperforms Mem0 and HippoRAG by 3.4% and 13.4% on episodic recollection and reasoning tasks respectively, with more robust refusal behavior.

problem: Molecular dynamics simulations are computationally expensive, limiting exploration of protein conformational landscapes.
approach: ProTDyn is a foundation protein language model that unifies conformational ensemble generation and multi-timescale dynamics modeling, enabling flexible i.i.d ensemble sampling and trajectory simulation.
contribution: Yields thermodynamically consistent ensembles, reproduces dynamical properties across multiple timescales, and generalizes to proteins beyond training data.

problem: RL post-training for reasoning produces depth-first brute-force traces rather than discovering reusable algorithmic procedures.
approach: RLAD jointly trains an abstraction generator and abstraction-conditioned solution generator via two-player RL, where models propose concise natural-language descriptions of procedures guiding solution generation.
contribution: Improves generalization to harder problems; spending test-time compute on abstraction generation proves more beneficial than generating more solutions at large inference budgets.

problem: Continual learning assumes memory is the limiting factor, but in practice GPU compute rather than storage is the bottleneck.
approach: Weight Space Consolidation combines rank-based parameter resets to restore plasticity with weight averaging to enhance stability, addressing the plasticity-stability tradeoff in high-memory regimes.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods while matching low computational cost of replay on class-incremental learning and continual instruction tuning.
theme: Transfer Learning, Meta Learning, and Lifelong Learning

problem: Heterogeneous features from agents with different sensing modalities complicate multi-agent collaborative perception and require retraining encoders or pairwise alignment.
approach: GT-Space constructs a common feature space from ground-truth labels providing unified alignment reference; agents project features via single adapter modules and fuse using contrastive losses.
contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines in detection accuracy on OPV2V, V2XSet simulation datasets and RCooper real-world dataset.

problem: Most graph learning datasets focus on small graphs for inductive tasks, offering limited insight into long-range dependencies in large graphs.
approach: City-Networks introduces large-scale transductive learning dataset derived from real-world city road networks with over 10^5 nodes and significantly larger diameters; a Jacobian-based measurement quantifies long-range dependencies.
contribution: Provides benchmark for evaluating long-range interactions and theoretical justifications based on over-smoothing and influence score dilution.

problem: LVLMs remain prone to hallucinations generating content inconsistent with visual evidence; existing methods overlook fine-grained token dynamics.
approach: AGE performs training-free layer-wise interventions by imitating attention patterns of real tokens: mimicking image attention and text attention when semantic grounding is required.
contribution: Consistently mitigates hallucinations across LVLMs like LLaVA, MiniGPT-4, and mPLUG-Owl2 without additional training or fluency loss on COCO, POPE, and MME benchmarks.

problem: VLA models use 2D encoders despite acting in 3D real-world environments, creating a spatial reasoning gap limiting generalization.
approach: FALCON injects rich 3D spatial tokens into the action head via spatial foundation models; an Embodied Spatial Model optionally fuses depth or pose without retraining.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on three simulation benchmarks and eleven real-world tasks, remaining robust under clutter, spatial conditioning, and scale variations.

problem: Graph optimization over unseen structures with constraints lacks principled Bayesian optimization frameworks.
approach: BoGrape builds on shortest-path graph kernels with mixed-integer programming formulation to enable global exploration over combinatorial graph domain with explicit constraint embedding.
contribution: Competitive performance on general synthetic benchmarks and representative molecular design case studies with application-specific constraints.

problem: System-level defenses against prompt injection appear costly in task completion but overlook reduced reliance on human oversight.
approach: A security-aware agent with richer HITL interactions explicitly plans for both task progress and policy compliance on top of information-flow control defense.
contribution: Achieves higher autonomy without sacrificing utility on AgentDojo and WASP benchmarks.

problem: LLMs treat numbers like word tokens, leading to frequency bias in embeddings and fragmentation across multiple tokens.
approach: FoNE directly maps numbers into embedding space using Fourier features, encoding each number as single token with two dimensions per digit.
contribution: Achieves higher accuracy on arithmetic, requires significantly less training data, and is only method achieving 100% accuracy on 100,000+ test examples; 64x less data needed for 6-digit addition.

problem: Two-sided matching platforms face imbalance where some users receive excess matches while others receive few and abandon, conflicting with retention goals.
approach: MRet (Matching for Retention) uses dynamic learning-to-rank modeling personalized retention curves, jointly optimizing retention gains for both recipients and recommended users.
contribution: Maximizes user retention as the ultimate objective, providing an alternative to match maximization or fairness-based approaches.

problem: Applying low-bit quantization to the Muon optimizer is underexplored due to difficulties from orthogonalization process and outlier patterns.
approach: 4-bit-Muon-GRASP uses grid quantization while preserving top singular subspace with minimal overhead to compress Muon states to 4 bits.
contribution: Achieves accuracy comparable to full-precision while reducing training memory consumption by up to 28% on LLaMA pre-training and fine-tuning tasks.

problem: Outcome-based RL for LLM reasoning is inefficient and credit assignment methods struggle to fairly evaluate step importance in partially correct chains.
approach: SSVPO uses Sequential Shapley Values measuring marginal contribution by reordering reasoning steps, identifying zero-credit steps and providing fair credit assignment with theoretical consistency to PPO.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art RL methods with up to 11.6% accuracy gain, 18.1% token reduction, and 1.6x efficiency improvement across 7 benchmarks.
